exposure: Gestational age at elective cesarean section
cohort: 7364 mothers with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies delivered by elective cesarean section at >=37 weeks gestation between 2002-2012.
finding: Infants born by elective cesarean section at lower gestational ages (specifically <39 weeks) had a higher rate of neonatal complications, including lower Apgar scores, hypoglycemia, hyperbilirubinemia, respiratory distress syndrome, and neonatal intensive care admissions.
